Less work while painting, loading pages, and starting up. Built with the HTML chrome enabled. Includes the download shelf from the same branch.

- Chrome is redrawn when something changed, instead of rebuilding the HTML UI on every paint.
- Ordinary blocked addresses are stopped in the network layer. The UI thread only sees the requests that still need a custom rule.
- The password vault stays closed until a login event. History, bookmarks, and session files are reread only when they change, and a visit is written once.
- Settings, history, and the split view are loaded when opened and released after they have been hidden. The Shield panel loads when its shortcut is used.
- YouTube player-ad stripping runs only on YouTube. Closing Windows or signing out flushes the last history and session write.
- Downloads can be opened from the toolbar and with Ctrl+J.

Uses less CPU, disk, and memory while idle, minimized, or opening the sidebar. Built with the HTML chrome enabled. Includes the v0.0.10 menu build.

- Page visits no longer rewrite the history file on the UI thread. A visit from the last moment before exit is still saved.
- Unchanged workspace and privacy files are not rewritten. Favicon files and the YouTube ad setting are reread only when they change.
- Minimizing hides the open pages so they stop drawing, and restoring shows them before the window lays out. The active tab is not suspended just because the window was minimized.
- A hidden sidebar web app drops to the low memory target. The idle memory check stops once the page is already in that state.
- The sidebar resizes the page once, at the end of the animation, instead of on every frame.
Submenus keep the menu opaque while the cards slide, so no white shows where the parent card was. Built with the HTML chrome enabled. Includes the v0.0.9 settings build.

The Privacy dashboard now lives inside Settings (Privacy and security) instead of its own window; Ctrl+Shift+Delete and the History page's Clear browsing data open it there. Toolbar reset sits in the card corner, and the blocker allow-list field and Make-default-browser button sit inline with their text. Clearing browsing data from Settings now works. Built with the HTML chrome enabled. Includes the v0.0.8 submenu build.

Submenus sit beside the row that opened them. Each child menu is its own card, only as tall as its buttons, and the parent eases aside. Built with the HTML chrome enabled. Includes the v0.0.7 customizability build.

Bowser Shield is built into the browser. The WebView2 request hook blocks ads and trackers with Bowser's own rules, and cosmetic rules are injected at the start of each page.

Installed copies follow `stable/release.json` on main. This asset is that pin: revision 3, SHA-256 `5baa4e5f1c5408bb483518d8cd2b91967b075f6c5fd361d651225abfe59d13da`.

Bowser 0.0.1 for 64-bit Windows 10 and 11.

Download **Bowser.exe** and open it. This build checks `stable/release.json` on GitHub after it has stayed open for about a minute, then at most once an hour. When that pin names a different file with a matching SHA-256, Bowser downloads it and switches on the next start. A build that fails to stay open is rolled back. Browser data stays in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Bowser`.

If you already downloaded an older Bowser.exe, download this file once, or run `Open-Bowser.cmd` from a clone. After that, the app keeps itself on the pinned build.

`Open-Bowser.cmd` installs this same file and adds Desktop and Start Menu shortcuts. It does not compile the source tree. Dev Bowser (`Dev-Bowser.cmd`) is a script in the repository for working on the source. It is not part of this download.

The [Evergreen WebView2 Runtime](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/#download-section) is required. Current Microsoft Edge already includes it.

This executable is not Authenticode-signed. SmartScreen may ask for More info, then Run anyway.
